title: Modal Title
prompt: A React modal can create or edit an item. Write a helper that returns "Create item" when mode is "create" and "Edit item" when mode is "edit".

explanation.beginner:
Example: modalTitle("create") produces "Create item". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “labels edit mode”: input ["edit"] produces "Edit item". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “labels edit mode”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
